A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Visual Word Tokenizer research despite the changed title. Their main text, appendices, figures, tables, and mathematical notation are readable and support reliable comparison across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original CLIP classification and subgroup-robustness results, BLIP captioning results, efficiency measurements, and main-text and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains original classification, robustness, captioning, and ablation results, and reports derived energy measurements and revised batching results.

M1.justification: Variance-based patch dropping and pixel-space clustering followed by cosine matching and embedding averaging remain unchanged. Combining VWT with quantization was already evaluated in v2 Appendix 7.2; its appearance in v4 Section 4.4 is a relocation.

E1.justification: Both versions use Waterbirds, CelebA, MetaShift, OpenImages common/rare subsets, COCO, NoCaps, and ImageNet-1K preprocessing. Classification, subgroup robustness, short- and long-form captioning, and online/offline inference coverage are retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Base, Q8, and ToMe, including Base and ToMe in the batching analysis. The VWT-plus-Q8 comparisons moved from v2 Table 10 to v4 Table 4 without changing their membership.

E3.justification: The central efficiency evaluation changes from separate power and runtime measures to energy in joules, calculated as power times runtime in seconds. The batching analysis also reports T_inter^100 instead of v2's T_inter^1000, retaining batch sizes 4, 8, 16, and 32. This establishes a reported setting change without establishing whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The batching ablation is revised to examine energy with a different reported inter-image vocabulary size. Embedding-space matching, random merging/dropping, threshold and dropping-ratio sensitivity, quantization compatibility, subgroup fairness, vocabulary sparsity, and captioning examples are otherwise retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The retained sample averages and vocabulary distributions do not introduce a change in uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v4 adds a central energy-results table: for example, COCO reports 2.39 J for Base and 1.26 J for T_inter^100. All 49 entries match products of the retained power/runtime values to reported precision. Figure 9 replaces batched power/runtime results with energy curves under the revised reported configuration. Matched task-performance tables remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The ViT and token-count formalism is unchanged, with no added assumptions, theorems, or proofs. The power-times-runtime calculation documents standard energy measurement rather than introducing new mathematical theory.

C1.justification: The headline claim changes from up to 25% lower wattage with at most 20% additional runtime to up to 47% lower energy consumption. Baseline comparisons now emphasize energy increases of 500% or more for Q8. The training-free tokenization contribution itself remains unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 acknowledges the larger MetaShift/OpenImages performance losses already visible in Table 3 and proposes foreground compression caused by less-uniform backgrounds as an explanation. It adds explicit medical-imaging/autonomous-driving applicability concerns and a tuning safeguard. The global-versus-local information guidance was already present in v2 and moves into the conclusion.

D1.justification: v4 explicitly identifies ImageNet-1K as preprocessing data for subsequent inter-image experiments, reports approximately 30–60 minutes of CPU vocabulary construction, and explains the energy calculation. These add documentation; the model sources, GPU, and public code access were already provided in v2.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 72 cited works and the same related-work positioning around efficient ViTs, specialized tokenizers, and vector quantization. Moving the quantization and distillation discussion into the main text adds no new research relationship.

P1.justification: v4 changes the title, rewrites the efficiency and performance narrative, consolidates Sections 4.3–4.9 into Experimental Results and Ablation Studies, and similarly reorganizes the supplementary experiments. Method-selection discussion moves into the conclusion, and captions receive substantial clarification.

P2.justification: v4 introduces the energy Table 2, moves the original power/runtime table to appendix Table 9, and promotes the quantization table into the main text. It transposes the threshold table, highlights VWT entries, and replaces Figure 9's six power/runtime panels with three energy panels, changing axes, legends, and appendix layout.

improvement.justification: v4 makes the efficiency comparison more meaningful by reporting energy while preserving the underlying single-image power/runtime measurements. Its discussion is also more candid about dataset-specific performance losses and information-loss limitations, with useful preprocessing details. These improve reporting and interpretation of largely unchanged experiments. Replacing the batching plots loses separate power/runtime detail, limiting the net gain.
